resolution: The prima via itself defines moving as educing from potency to act (claim AQUINAS-ST-I-Q2-A3-REDUCED-BY-A-MOVER-A), and the case reads motus in that broad sense. Aristotle's physical change is one kind of such reduction, so the observation premise STMT-SOMETHING-IS-MOVED-IN-THIS-WORLD holds on either reading. All premises share `MovedIn`/`MovesIn` over an abstract `Respect`, so the formal results hold for any one reading applied throughout; an objection that the regress premises hold only for local motion is an objection to a premise, not an equivocation. Scope (#404): the typed Physics readings (TruthCore.Greek.Aristotle.Physics.Typed, docs/typed-physics.md) read `MovedIn`/`MovesIn` as physical motion. A universal prima via premise restricts to physical motion, so results that use prima via premises to derive typed Physics statements stay within one reading. The converse does not hold: Physics premises about physical motion do not extend to every reduction from potency to act. VIII.4's division and its conclusions therefore carry an explicit guard for respects of physical motion (`IsPhysicalRespect`, DEF-PHYSICAL-RESPECT); its other readings are scoped by their antecedent primitives (forced, natural, self-, passive natural motion are kinds of physical motion by definition); the III.3 and VIII.5 readings carry no guard and are accepted only under a physical instantiation of `MovedIn`/`MovesIn`. The VIII.4 readings yield STMT-EVERY-PHYSICAL-MOTION-HAS-A-PER-SE-MOVER. They reach the root premise STMT-NOTHING-REDUCED-TO-ACT-EXCEPT-BY-A-MOVER only through the explicit, unattributed scope premise STMT-EVERY-REDUCTION-TO-ACT-IS-PHYSICAL-MOTION (result ARIST-PHYS-VIII-4-SCOPE-BRIDGE-TO-PRIMA-VIA), which is open and false on the broad reading if some reduction is not a physical motion. BRIDGE-ARIST-MOTION-ANALYSIS-MOVED-AS-IN-POTENCY reads Physics III.1's definition (STMT-BEING-MOVED-IS-ACTUALIZATION-OF-POTENCY) with the same `MovedIn` as STMT-NOTHING-MOVED-EXCEPT-AS-IN-POTENCY. Aristotle states the definition for physical change; applied to the broad reading it is the definition extended to every reduction from potency to act, and the bridge carries his support to the premise only as far as that extension holds. Moving as an end (#352): Met. XII.7's unmoved mover moves as an object of love (ὡς ἐρώμενον, 1072b3; In Metaph. XII, lect. 7 n. 1-3, sicut desiderabile, the heaven's motion being for its sake and caused by a proximate mover). The Lambda.7 readings (STMT-SOME-UNMOVED-MOVER-CANNOT-BE-OTHERWISE, STMT-EVERY-UNMOVED-MOVER-CANNOT-BE-OTHERWISE) read the case's MovesIn to include moving as an end: on the broad reading, what moves as an end is that for whose sake a potency is reduced to act. This is an unattributed reading choice, not a claim that Aristotle's mover is an efficient mover. ARIST-MET-XII-7-FIRST-MOVER-PURE-ACT depends on it: its uniqueness step identifies the prima via's first mover with Lambda.7's mover through the same MovesIn. If MovesIn is read as efficient moving only, the Lambda.7 mover need not satisfy IsFirstUnmovedMover and the step fails. Lambda.7's 'unmoved' and 'in no way otherwise' are read over the respects of change (DEF-RESPECT-OF-CHANGE); their extension to every respect, for a mover that moves something and is unmoved and unable to be otherwise in every respect of change, is the unattributed STMT-UNCHANGEABLE-IN-RESPECTS-OF-CHANGE-IS-UNCHANGEABLE-SIMPLY.
